**Apprentissage chaud / Apprentissage fr: **Hot Learning / Cold Learning**: This parameter indicates the progress of the learning process. A value of 1 indicates the start of learning, during which the algorithm performs a rough adjustment of the coefficients. As this parameter increases, the adjustment becomes more refined. A value of 50 indicates the end of learning.
**Apprentissage isolation chaud / Appren: **Heat Insulation Learning / Cold Insulation Learning**: Same function as above, but for insulation coefficients.
**Chauffage seulement** : la régulation: **Heating only**: the control system operates only for heating
**Climatisation seulement** : la régulat: **Cooling only**: the control system is active only for cooling
**Coefficient de chauffage / Coefficient: **Heating Coefficient / Cooling Coefficient**: This represents the gain of the control system. This value is multiplied by the difference between the setpoint and the measured indoor temperature to calculate the heating/cooling time.
**Delta consigne - température extérieur: **Delta setpoint - outdoor temperature for heating/cooling mode**: The thermostat selects the mode (heating or cooling) based on the setpoint and the outdoor temperature (for energy-saving purposes, we assume that the indoor temperature tends to match the outdoor temperature). You can use these settings to adjust the threshold. Ex: If you want 25 and it’s 22 outside, by default the thermostat will switch to heating mode (it’s just entering this mode for the calculation—it doesn’t mean it will actually heat), but if you set the heating delta to 4, it will no longer heat because 25–22 = 3 and 3 < 4, so it will switch to cooling mode (provided, of course, that the indoor temperature is higher than the setpoint).
**Delta consigne** : uniquement disponib: **Setpoint Delta**: Available only in timer mode, this command allows you to enter a calculation delta for the setpoint. If the value is greater than 0, the thermostat will check whether it needs to heat to (setpoint - delta/2); if so, it will heat up to (setpoint + delta/2). The benefit is that the system heats for longer periods but less frequently.
**Isolation chauffage / Isolation clim**: **Heating/Cooling Insulation**: This coefficient is multiplied by the difference between the setpoint and the measured outdoor temperature to calculate the heating/cooling time. It represents the contribution of the outdoor temperature to the heating/cooling time, and its value is typically lower than the heating/cooling coefficient in the case of a well-insulated room.
**Les modes** : il est possible de faire: **Modes**: You can switch between modes by directly executing the commands (here: Comfort, Morning Comfort, Eco, Vacation).
**Limite les cycles marche/arrêt incessa: **Limits constant on/off cycling (wood pellets, natural gas, heating oil) and PID**: This option allows for control using different heat levels. The power feedback from the next cycle must provide the new heat level setpoint to the heating unit. Cycles end at 100%, so the cycle time must be short.
**Marge de défaillance chaud / Marge de: **Heating Failure Margin / Cooling Failure Margin**: This value is used to detect a malfunction in the heating or cooling system. When the temperature deviates from the setpoint by more than this margin for more than 3 consecutive cycles, the thermostat switches to heating failure mode.
**Off** : cette commande coupe le thermo: **Off**: This command turns off the thermostat; control is no longer active, and the heating/air conditioning is turned off
**Offset chauffage(%) / Offset clim(%)**: **Heating Offset (%) / Cooling Offset (%)**: The heating offset accounts for *internal heat gains*; normally, it should not be a fixed value, but we assume that the learning process incorporates the dynamic component into the other two coefficients. *Internal heat sources* include, for example, a computer that raises the temperature when turned on, but they can also include people (1 person = 80 W on average) and the refrigerator in the kitchen. In a south-facing room, a sunlit facade can provide additional heat. In theory, this coefficient is negative.
**Offset chauffage** : modifie le coeffi: **Heating Offset**: Adjusts the heating offset coefficient corresponding to internal heat gains; a scenario can modify this setting based on a presence detector, for example
**Offset froid** : comme ci-dessus mais: **Cooling offset**: same as above, but for air conditioning
**Offset à appliquer si le radiateur est: **Offset to apply if the radiator is considered hot (%)**: Use this setting if your heating control system has significant thermal inertia, whether due to the radiators, the room layout (distance between the radiator and the temperature sensor), or the temperature sensor itself (depending on the model, their responsiveness varies). The visible consequence of this thermal inertia is a temporary overshoot of the setpoint during significant temperature increases (for example, when the setpoint changes from 15°C to 19°C). This parameter corresponds to the observed delay between the heating period (= the heater is on) and the period when the temperature measured by the sensor begins to rise, divided by the configured cycle length. For example, if there is a 30-minute delay between the start of heating and the start of the temperature rise, and the heating cycle duration is set to 60 minutes, this parameter can be set to 50%. Thus, when a 100% heating cycle is followed by another heating cycle, this parameter allows the system to account for the heat generated by the radiator during the first cycle—but not yet measured by the sensor—when calculating the second cycle, by reducing its heating power accordingly. The power of the second cycle will then be reduced by 50% compared to the calculation based on the temperature measured by the sensor.
**Performance** : uniquement disponible: **Performance**: Available only if you have an outdoor temperature sensor and an energy consumption command (in kWh, reset to 0 every day at 12:00 a.m.). This feature shows you the performance of your heating system relative to the unified degree-day index.
**Puissance** : uniquement disponible en: **Power**: Available only in timer mode, this command specifies the percentage of heating/cooling time relative to the total cycle time.
**Smart start** : Cette option permet de: **Smart Start**: This option adds intelligence to the thermostat by anticipating changes to the setpoint so that the desired temperature is reached at the scheduled time. This option requires the calendar plugin. Please note that for Smart Start to work, the learning value must be greater than 25. Also, it only takes into account the event that is closest in time.
**Temps de chauffe minimum (% du cycle)*: **Minimum heating time (% of cycle)**: If the calculation results in a heating time shorter than this value, the thermostat determines that heating or cooling is not necessary, and the command will defer to the next cycle. This helps prevent damage to certain appliances, such as stoves, and also ensures true energy efficiency.
**Thermostat** : il s’agit de la consign: **Thermostat**: This refers to the thermostat's setpoint.
**Tout autorisé** : modifie le comportem: **All allowed**: changes the thermostat's behavior so that it operates in both heating and cooling modes
**cycle (min)** : il s’agit du cycle de: **Cycle (min)**: This refers to the thermostat’s calculation cycle. At the end of the cycle, based on the difference between the actual temperatures and the setpoint, the thermostat calculates the heating time for the next cycle.

**unlock** : déverrouille le thermostat: **unlock**: Unlocks the thermostat, allowing you to change its status

Le thermostat déclenche une défaillance: The thermostat triggers a sensor fault if the last temperature reading is too old, if the indoor temperature is below the minimum or above the maximum setpoint, or if the value is invalid. When the fault occurs, it is possible to set the device to a predetermined mode, such as forcing a pilot-wire radiator to operate. More simply, sending a text message or notification allows you to be alerted and take manual action.
Le verrou présent sur le widget permet d: The lock on the widget allows you to lock the thermostat at a specific setpoint in case of unforeseen circumstances, such as vacations, guests, etc.
Existing actions are retained. A persistent fault does not trigger the actions again at every check; the occurrence of a new cause triggers them only once, accompanied by a message listing all active faults. A return to normal resets each cause separately. Checks for timeouts and invalid values are shared by the time-based and hysteresis engines; exceeding the min/max limits continues to trigger their actions during periodic checks.
Les actions sont celles qui permettent d: Actions are commands that allow you to heat, cool (air conditioning), or stop the system. An additional action can be set to occur whenever the setpoint changes, whether in manual or automatic mode.
Les défaillances peuvent provenir soit d: Failures can originate either from the temperature sensors or from the heating command system. The thermostat may detect a fault if the temperature deviates from the setpoint for an extended period.
Les modes (définis dans l’onglet **Modes: Modes (defined in the **Modes** tab) are preset thermostat settings that match your lifestyle. For example, *Night* or *Eco* mode sets the temperature you want when everyone is asleep. *Day* or *Comfort* mode determines how the thermostat operates to maintain a comfortable temperature when you’re at home. Nothing here is set in stone. You can define as many modes as you like and use them via scenarios (we’ll come back to this later).

cumul du temps de chauffe du thermostat: cumulative heating time of the thermostat
donnez un nom à ce mode, par exemple: Give this mode a name, for example
définition du moteur de thermostat (hyst: Definition of the thermostat control mechanism (hysteresis or time-based). This refers to the choice of control algorithm.
la configuration et la plage de fonction: Configuration and operating range: heating only, air conditioning, or both; minimum and maximum operating temperatures.
la gestion des défaillances des équipeme: management of equipment failures, temperature sensors, and heating devices,
la possibilité de gérer les ouvrants pou: the ability to control the windows to turn off the thermostat,
la prise en compte de la température ext: taking into account the outdoor temperature, and therefore the home’s insulation coefficient,
le mode **hystérésis** correspond à l’al: **Hysteresis** mode involves turning the heating on and off based on the indoor temperature relative to a threshold corresponding to the setpoint. Hysteresis helps prevent the system from cycling on and off too frequently when the temperature is near the setpoint.
le mode **temporel** calcule un pourcent: The **time-based** mode calculates a heating percentage based on a predefined time cycle, taking into account the differences between the setpoint and the indoor and outdoor temperatures (insulation). This mode is more accurate and features a learning function that automatically adjusts the coefficients, but it may require some manual adjustments to adapt it to your system. Important: For the time-based mode to work, you must have both an indoor AND an outdoor temperature sensor.
sélectionnez l’info du capteur d’ouvertu: Select the information from the opening sensor in the field
sélectionnez une action et remplissez le: select an action and fill in the associated fields
un autre graphique qui affiche les courb: Another graph showing the setpoint curves, indoor temperature, and heating status.
un graphique représentant le cumul du te: a graph showing the cumulative heating time per day (in hours),
un système de régulation qui apprend pou: a control system that learns to optimize control,
une programmation complète avec le plugi: Comprehensive scheduling with the calendar plugin, including the ability to set the target temperature in advance so that it is reached at the scheduled time (Smartstart)
